facts.value: International students who wish to pursue their studies at ASU must obtain an F-1 or J-1 visa.
facts.programme_association: African and African American Studies - BA

facts.value: To obtain a visa, students must first receive a SEVIS number and I-20 document from ASU.
facts.programme_association: African and African American Studies - BA

facts.value: ASU guides each student through the process of obtaining their I-20 using the I-20 Tracker in My ASU.
facts.programme_association: African and African American Studies - BA

facts.value: Through My ASU Parent Guest Access, you can share your academic records with your parent or guardian and give them access to pay your tuition and bills.
facts.programme_association: African and African American Studies - BA

facts.value: Pay your enrollment deposit through My ASU to confirm you will attend.
facts.programme_association: African and African American Studies - BA

facts.value: For fall 2026 admits, the enrollment deposit will be available beginning Oct. 1, 2025.
facts.programme_association: African and African American Studies - BA

facts.value: All first-year students are required to take the math placement test at least seven calendar days before their Academic Orientation Session.
facts.programme_association: African and African American Studies - BA

facts.value: You will see the item 'Take Math Placement Test' under Priority Tasks in My ASU.
